Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

opera noun

also operas, opera house, go to the opera, operatic, overture

modern

Traupman 52: melodrāma vīsere, go to see an opera

melodrāma, melodrāmatis n.

noun, third declension

an opera

Traupman’s word, Greek μελόδραμα, a play with song; his melodrāmatium is an operetta or a musical (see musical). In English a melodrama is something else.

Other words

  • drāma mūsicum — an opera

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. works: opera

    Morgan–Owens, after Egger; drāma itself is late (Ausonius, Lewis & Short).

  • ōdēum, ōdēī n. — an opera house, a concert hall

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Vitr. 5.9; Suet. Dom. 5 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. concert hall: opera house

    The Greek odeon, a roofed building for music.

  • theātrum melodrāmāticum

See also theatre, concert, musical, music.
